findings.title: Pay-If-Paid Clause
findings.subtitle: Payment is contingent on GC receiving funds from Owner
findings.excerpt: …payment to Subcontractor is expressly conditioned upon General Contractor's receipt of payment from the City of Charleston Owner…
findings.explain: A pay-if-paid clause makes your right to payment entirely contingent on the GC receiving payment from the Owner. If the Owner doesn't pay — for any reason — you get nothing, even if your flooring work was perfect.
findings.scNote: South Carolina courts enforce clearly-written pay-if-paid clauses as a complete defense to payment. Cite: Shelco, Inc. v. Alanthus Corp.
findings.counter: Strike or replace with: "Payment to Subcontractor is not contingent upon General Contractor's receipt of payment from Owner. In no event shall payment be delayed more than 45 days from Subcontractor's invoice date."
actions: Strike this clause or replace with a pay-when-paid provision with a 45-day backstop
Price the job 5–10% higher to account for payment risk if clause cannot be removed

findings.title: Broad Indemnification — Potentially Void Under SC Law
findings.subtitle: May require covering GC's own negligence — illegal in SC
findings.excerpt: …Subcontractor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the General Contractor and Owner from any and all claims arising out of or in connection with Subcontractor's Work…
findings.explain: Broad indemnification clauses attempt to shift ALL liability to you — including claims caused by the GC's own negligence.
findings.scNote: S.C. Code § 32-2-10 voids any provision requiring a subcontractor to indemnify the GC for the GC's OWN negligence.
findings.counter: Replace with: "Subcontractor's indemnity is limited to claims arising from Subcontractor's own negligence, per S.C. Code § 32-2-10."

findings.title: Unconditional Lien Waiver Required
findings.subtitle: Waiving lien rights BEFORE receiving payment
findings.excerpt: …as a condition of each progress payment, Subcontractor shall provide an unconditional lien waiver covering all labor and materials…
findings.explain: An unconditional lien waiver permanently releases your right to file a mechanics' lien the moment you sign it — even if you haven't been paid.
findings.scNote: Under SC Mechanics' Lien Law (§29-5-10), always use CONDITIONAL lien waivers.
findings.counter: Require conditional waivers only: "Any lien waiver shall be effective solely upon Subcontractor's actual receipt and clearance of the specified payment."
actions: NEVER sign unconditional waiver until check clears

findings.title: 10% Retainage
findings.subtitle: High retainage ties up significant cash flow
findings.excerpt: …Owner shall retain ten percent (10%) of the value of each progress payment…
findings.explain: 10% retainage on a $200,000 job means $20,000 sitting with the GC, potentially for months.
findings.scNote: SC Code § 11-35-3030 limits retainage on public projects to 6%.
findings.counter: Negotiate: "Retainage shall not exceed 5%. Releases within 30 days of punch-list completion."
actions: Decouple your retainage release from overall project completion

findings.title: Additional Insured Requirement
findings.subtitle: GC and Owner named on your policy — verify coverage
findings.excerpt: …Subcontractor shall name the Owner and General Contractor as additional insureds on a primary and non-contributory basis…
findings.explain: Standard practice, but you need to confirm your insurer will add them and understand any premium costs.
findings.scNote: Additional insured status must be endorsed explicitly.
findings.counter: Call your insurance broker before signing to confirm the endorsement and any added premium.
actions: Call your insurance broker before signing
Obtain the COI before starting work

findings.title: Pay-If-Paid Clause
findings.subtitle: Payment contingent on Owner paying GC
findings.excerpt: …receipt of payment from Owner is a condition precedent to Subcontractor's right to payment hereunder…
findings.explain: A pay-if-paid clause makes your right to payment entirely contingent on the GC receiving payment from the Owner.
findings.scNote: SC courts enforce clearly-written pay-if-paid clauses. Cite: Shelco, Inc. v. Alanthus Corp.
findings.counter: Strike or replace with a 45-day backstop payment provision.

findings.title: No Damages for Delay Clause
findings.subtitle: GC can delay your work with no financial compensation
findings.excerpt: …Subcontractor's sole remedy for any delay or disruption shall be an extension of time and Subcontractor waives all claims for delay damages…
findings.explain: Even if the GC's mismanagement idles your crew for weeks, your only remedy is more time — not money.
findings.scNote: SC recognizes exceptions for active interference and bad faith. Document all GC-caused delays immediately.
findings.counter: Negotiate carve-outs for GC-caused delays exceeding 14 consecutive days.

findings.title: Broad Indemnification
findings.subtitle: Covers GC's own negligence — void under SC § 32-2-10
findings.excerpt: …Subcontractor shall indemnify and hold harmless the General Contractor from any and all claims, including those arising from General Contractor's own acts or omissions…
findings.explain: This clause explicitly requires you to indemnify the GC for the GC's own negligence — which is void under SC law.
findings.scNote: S.C. Code § 32-2-10 makes this provision void as against public policy.
findings.counter: Cite § 32-2-10 and demand removal of the GC's own negligence language.

findings.title: Broad Prime Contract Flow-Down
findings.subtitle: Bound by a contract you haven't seen
findings.excerpt: …Subcontractor is bound by all terms of the Prime Contract between the County and General Contractor, which is hereby incorporated by reference…
findings.explain: Flow-down clauses make you responsible for every obligation in the GC's contract with the Owner.
findings.scNote: SC courts enforce flow-down clauses even if you never received a copy of the prime contract.
findings.counter: Require a full copy of the prime contract before signing. Limit flow-down to safety, insurance, and warranty only.
actions: Request and read the prime contract before signing

findings.title: 48-Hour Claims Notice Window
findings.subtitle: Missing notice deadlines voids your claims
findings.excerpt: …any claim for additional time or compensation must be submitted in writing within 48 hours of the event giving rise to such claim…
findings.explain: A 48-hour notice window means that if you're busy in the field and miss the deadline, you forfeit a legitimate claim entirely.
findings.scNote: SC courts enforce notice provisions strictly. Do not rely on waiver defenses.
findings.counter: Negotiate to 7 business days minimum.
actions: Assign one person to track and send all written notices

findings.title: 10% Retainage
findings.subtitle: Significant cash flow impact
findings.excerpt: …ten percent (10%) of the amount of each Application for Payment shall be retained…
findings.explain: 10% retainage creates serious cash flow problems on large projects.
findings.scNote: SC public projects are limited to 6% retainage by statute.
findings.counter: Negotiate to 5% with early release at substantial completion.
actions: Decouple your retainage from overall project completion

findings.title: Waiver of Subrogation
findings.subtitle: Standard provision — confirm with your broker
findings.excerpt: …each party waives all rights of subrogation against the other…
findings.explain: Standard and generally acceptable. Confirm with your insurance broker.
findings.scNote: Most SC policies accommodate this for little or no added cost.
findings.counter: Acceptable. Notify your broker to add the endorsement.

findings.title: Broad Indemnification
findings.subtitle: Covers losses beyond Subcontractor's own fault
findings.excerpt: …Subcontractor shall indemnify and save harmless the Owner and its officers, agents, and employees from all losses and claims arising out of Subcontractor's work…
findings.explain: This indemnification language is broad enough to potentially sweep in claims beyond your own fault.
findings.scNote: S.C. Code § 32-2-10 limits enforceability to your own negligence only.
findings.counter: Narrow to: "Subcontractor indemnifies for claims arising solely from Subcontractor's own negligence."

findings.title: Written Change Order Requirement
findings.subtitle: Verbal field instructions may not be compensable
findings.excerpt: …no additional compensation shall be due for changes in Work unless a written Change Order has been executed prior to commencement of changed work…
findings.explain: Any verbal instruction to do extra work may not be compensable without prior written approval.
findings.scNote: SC courts enforce written change order requirements strictly.
findings.counter: Add deemed-approval provision: GC silence for 5 days = approved.
actions: Create a field change authorization form
Follow verbal instructions with same-day email confirmation

findings.title: 10% Retainage
findings.subtitle: High retainage on what could be a mid-sized flooring job
findings.excerpt: …the Owner shall retain ten percent (10%) of the value of the Contractor's last payment…
findings.explain: 10% retainage creates cash flow pressure, especially if release is tied to overall project completion.
findings.scNote: SC public projects capped at 6% retainage by statute.
findings.counter: Negotiate to 5% with release at YOUR substantial completion.
actions: Decouple your retainage from total project

findings.title: 21-Day Claims Notice Requirement
findings.subtitle: Claims must be filed within 21 days or are waived
findings.excerpt: …Claims must be initiated within twenty-one (21) days after occurrence of the event giving rise to such Claim. By failing to give written notice within the time required, a party expressly waives its Claim…
findings.explain: 21 days is better than 24–48 hours, but still requires a system to track and file claims on time.
findings.scNote: SC courts enforce contractual notice provisions. This mirrors the City of Charleston's own standard contract language.
findings.counter: Acceptable if you have a tracking system. Add: "Notice defects shall not bar a claim if GC had actual knowledge."
actions: Assign one person responsible for all written notices

findings.title: Waiver of Subrogation
findings.subtitle: Standard provision
findings.excerpt: …each party waives all rights against the other for damages covered by property insurance…
findings.explain: Standard and generally acceptable in SC.
findings.scNote: Confirm with your broker before work begins.
findings.counter: Acceptable provision. Notify broker.

findings.title: Additional Insured Requirement
findings.subtitle: Verify your policy can accommodate
findings.excerpt: …Subcontractor shall supply a written endorsement naming the Owner as additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis…
findings.explain: Standard practice — confirm your insurer will issue the endorsement and what it costs.
findings.scNote: Additional insured endorsement must be explicit in the policy.
findings.counter: Call your broker before signing.

findings.title: 10% Retainage
findings.subtitle: Standard for public works but negotiable
findings.excerpt: …ten percent (10%) retainage shall be withheld from each progress payment…
findings.explain: 10% retainage is common on public road projects but SC statute limits it to 6%.
findings.scNote: SC Code § 11-35-3030 limits public project retainage to 6%.
findings.counter: Negotiate to comply with SC statutory maximum of 6%.

findings.title: Waiver of Subrogation
findings.subtitle: Standard provision
findings.excerpt: …parties mutually waive rights of subrogation against each other…
findings.explain: Standard and acceptable. Confirm with your broker.
findings.scNote: Most SC policies accommodate this.
findings.counter: Acceptable. Notify broker.
